procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
procedural_history.impugned_order: Final judgment and order dated 05.12.2014 passed by the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in Writ-C.No.46342 of 2013
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court allowed a writ petition (WC No. 46342 of 2013), confirming an earlier order. The High Court found that Respondent Nos. 5 and 6 had unauthorizedly constructed commercial shops on residential property and sold them to the appellants. The High Court ordered demolition of the unauthorized construction and directed criminal and departmental action against erring officials.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellants, who are third parties to the High Court proceedings (purchasers of the unauthorized commercial shops), challenged the High Court's order in the Supreme Court via Civil Appeal No. 14604 of 2024 (and likely Civil Appeal No. 14605 of 2024). The Supreme Court initially granted permission to file a special leave petition, issued notice, and ordered a status quo. Ultimately, the Supreme Court dismissed the appeals, confirming the High Court's order.

directions: The order of the High Court shall stand confirmed.
With the aforesaid observations and directions, these appeals stand dismissed.
There is no order as to costs.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

issue.issue_text: as to whether the unauthorized construction is compoundable, if it is not so, the reasons therefor

facts: The case involved unauthorized construction by Respondent No. 5, which was found to be deliberate, designed, and motivated, rather than marginal or accidental.
The respondents (No. 5 and 6) stated they had no objection to the demolition of the unauthorized construction.
The High Court had previously ordered the demolition of the structure.
law: The Supreme Court has established in a series of decisions that the illegality of an unauthorized construction cannot be perpetuated.
Construction made in contravention of Acts/Rules is illegal and must be demolished.
Such constructions cannot be legitimized or protected under the excuse of passage of time, inaction of authorities, or the substantial money spent on them.
Courts must deal with unauthorized constructions with an "iron hand," and any leniency is considered misplaced sympathy.
Administrative failures, regulatory inefficiency, or negligence by authorities cannot be used as a defense to protect illegal constructions.
Regularization of violations is not a right and should only be considered in exceptional circumstances, not as a means for the state to generate revenue.
application: The Court applied the principle that illegal constructions must be demolished, especially when the violations are deliberate and significant, as they were in this case.
The Court found that since the violations did not qualify for regularization under the law, demolition was the correct course of action.
The Court affirmed the High Court's demolition order, finding no reason to interfere with it, especially given that the respondents did not object to the demolition.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court accepted that unauthorized construction is not compoundable. It held that such constructions are illegal, cannot be perpetuated, and must be demolished. The Court reasoned that allowing these structures to be regularized or protected through excuses like money spent, administrative inaction, or passage of time would undermine the rule of law. Therefore, a strict approach is required, and demolition is the necessary consequence for constructions that violate building plans and regulations.

respondent_arguments: The respondent authorities (Respondents Nos. 2 to 4) supported the case of Respondent No. 1 and submitted that they are ready to provide all protection and facilities to demolish the unauthorized construction as ordered by the High Court.

cases.case_name: Municipal Corporation, Ludhiana v. Inderjeet Singh
cases.principle: If a proper show-cause notice had been served before a demolition order, the recipient could have had the opportunity to show that the alleged violation was of a negligible character that did not warrant demolition.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: Constructions put up in violation of or deviation from an approved building plan, or without any approval, cannot be encouraged. Factors such as delay, administrative failure, regulatory inefficiency, cost of construction, investment, or negligence by authorities cannot be used as a shield to defend action taken against illegal constructions. Judicial discretion cannot be exercised to encourage or perpetuate an illegality; an unauthorized construction that is illegal and cannot be compounded must be demolished.
obiter: State Governments often seek to enrich themselves through the process of regularisation by condoning/ratifying the violations and illegalities.
All unauthorized constructions have to be dealt with in same manner.
The fact that a party has put up a permanent structure is not relevant if the same has been done on a plot of land allotted in contravention of law.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: An unauthorized construction, if it is illegal and cannot be compounded under the law, must be demolished. Courts have no judicial discretion to allow such a structure to stand, as such discretion cannot be exercised to encourage or perpetuate an illegality. The principle that no consideration should be shown to a builder who has engaged in unauthorized construction is a dicta that is now almost bordering on the rule of law.
legal_tests_applied: If an unauthorized construction is illegal and cannot be compounded, it has to be demolished. There is no way out.
why_appellant_lost: The argument that a permanent structure has already been built is not relevant, as the construction was done on a plot of land allotted in contravention of law.

Judicial discretion cannot be guided by expediency or be used to encourage or perpetuate an illegality. Justice must be rendered in accordance with law, and courts are not free from statutory fetters.
The court cannot exercise equitable jurisdiction for the regularization of illegal and unauthorized constructions, as this would enable violators to retain the results of their illegal acts.
why_respondent_won: The High Court's order of demolition was correct as the court found no valid reason to interfere with it, especially considering that even some respondents had no objection to the demolition.

The demolition of illegal construction enforces the performance of a statutory duty by public bodies, which is an obligation to ratepayers and residents who have a legal right to demand compliance and whose interests are injured by the illegal construction.
policy_considerations: No authority administrating municipal laws and other similar laws can encourage violation of the sanctioned plan.

In the larger public interest, courts are expected to refrain from exercising equitable jurisdiction for regularisation of illegal and unauthorised constructions so as to enable the violators to retain the results of their illegal acts.

The Court enforces the performance of statutory duty by public bodies as obligation to rate payers who have a legal right to demand compliance by a local authority with its duty to observe statutory rights alone. The scheme here is for the benefit of the public. There is special interest in the performance of the duty.
